speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea; to help identify the cause, please tell me if you have had any recent travel, exposure to sick contacts, or changes in your diet recently. Additionally, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea or constipation?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old female. The patient describes a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. She recalls attending the state fair over a month ago where she tried various regional foods. Recently, she has observed the darkening of her urine, which she believes is due to inadequate water intake. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That state fair visit raises concern for foodborne illness; has your abdominal pain been specifically in the right upper quadrant, and have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes? Also, are you experiencing clay-colored stools or jaundice?

REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel, Complete_Blood_Count, Urinalysis
REQUEST IMAGES: Right_upper_quadrant_ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver_Function_Panel: Total_Bilirubin_3.6_mg/dL, Direct_Bilirubin_2.4_mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase_72_U/L, AST_488_U/L, ALT_798_U/L; Complete_Blood_Count: Hemoglobin_10.6_g/dL, Leukocyte_Count_11600/mm3, Platelet_Count_221000/mm3; Urinalysis: Not_provided_in_data (Note: Clinical presentation suggests dark urine due to bilirubinuria).

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and mild fever. I also have Abdominal pain, Nausea, Dark urine. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis.

While the previous mention of appendicitis is noted, the clinical picture of fatigue, fever, nausea, right upper quadrant pain, and specifically dark urine is highly characteristic of liver inflammation rather than appendicitis. Your urine analysis and liver function tests, which I have already ordered, will confirm this. Please do not proceed with any surgery until these results are back.
